notes: The planned 2024-01 to 2026-09 series could not be built, and no y/y growth was computed. pypistats keeps only about 180 days of history, so the ugbio-core API returned Apr–Oct 2026 only (ugbio-core is one of the Ultima packages, and the other Ultima and Element packages were not queried). The Docker Hub API returns one cumulative pull_count with no time series, and the Wayback lookup I tried returned 404. Anaconda.org URLs for bioconda bases2fastq and bcl-convert returned 404 (both the API and the package page), so no Bioconda counts. I did not test other package names, and BigQuery pypi stats or the clickhouse pypi dataset were not tried. The counts also include CI and mirror traffic. The 2026 figures are real but have no baseline, they don't separate lab use from CI, and they don't compare against an Illumina tool. They are therefore not usable as thesis evidence.
how_to_mine: Bioconda: the package page and API URLs I tried returned 404, so check the exact package names (e.g. 'bases2fastq' may live under another channel) or use the anaconda-package-data parquet on GitHub or the AWS public dataset (monthly per-package counts since 2017). PyPI history: run the public BigQuery pypi dataset or the clickhouse pypi_downloads dataset, for ugbio-core, ugbio-*, ugvc and any Element Python packages. Docker Hub: poll pull_count monthly from now on, since only cumulative values are available. Compare against bcl-convert only on Bioconda, because Illumina distributes it mainly via its own installer.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Ultima's open-source analysis package ugbio-core is downloaded about 6–8K times a month on PyPI in mid-2026, but there is no baseline to show growth.
items.detail: pypistats shows ugbio-core at 5,784 downloads in May 2026, 8,432 in Jun, 8,135 in Jul and 7,849 in Aug, all with mirrors. Without mirrors the figures are 3,731, 6,430, 6,386 and 5,681. Elembio/bases2fastq on Docker Hub shows 16,954 cumulative pulls since it was registered on 2022-04-14. These counts include CI and mirror traffic and have no Illumina or prior-year comparison, so they can't show how many labs run rival platforms.
items.why_new: This is the first download-count read on the rival short-read tool ecosystem. It has no trend, though, so it only sets a baseline.

new_candidates.source: anaconda-package-data parquet or BigQuery pypi dataset
new_candidates.why: They hold multi-year monthly counts that would allow a y/y comparison, which the live APIs here can't give.
